=== README ===
# SSH Key Backup Inventory

Source: `C:\Users\19y\.ssh` · Tidied: 2026-10-15 · Repo visibility: **private**

> **WARNING — this archive contains private keys.** Anyone with access to this
> repository or to any clone/copy of it can authenticate to the servers listed in
> `server_list.txt`. If the repo is ever made public, or the GitHub token that
> pushes it leaks, treat *every* key and *every* password below as compromised and
> rotate them. See [Security notes](#security-notes) first.

## ⚠️ Security notes (read before sharing this repo)

1. `server_list.txt` stores **plaintext root passwords** for six hosts:
   `156.245.245.197` (hk), `localhost:2222` (wsl), `sshwh.ccmii.eu.org` (aliwh root),
   `23.141.204.202` (FRONT), `192.168.1.20` (company), `192.168.1.1`.
   These are committed in git history (commits `15ac677` and earlier), so removing the
   lines in a new commit does **not** remove them from the repo. Rotating the passwords
   is the only real fix; rewriting history (`git filter-repo`) plus a force-push would
   be needed to purge the file itself.
2. `192.168.1.20` / `192.168.1.1` are LAN addresses belonging to a former workplace
   network. There is no reason for company credentials to sit in a personal GitHub repo.
3. Seven of the ten private keys are stored **without a passphrase**, so the file alone
   is a complete credential. The three that are passphrase-protected are marked below.

## Line endings matter (why `.gitattributes` exists)

Windows OpenSSH **refuses to load** an OpenSSH private key whose lines end in CRLF —
`ssh-keygen` reports `error in libcrypto` and `ssh` falls back to password auth. Before
this tidy-up, every file in `keys/` except `moe_ed25519` was CRLF and therefore *did not
work if restored as-is*. All files are now LF, and `.gitattributes` (`* text eol=lf`)
pins that so future checkouts and editors cannot convert them back.

Verify after any checkout:

```powershell
ssh-keygen -lf .\keys\aliwh_ed25519          # must print a SHA256: fingerprint
```

## Keys (`keys/`)

All ten are ED25519. Every private key parses and every `.pub` matches its private key
(fingerprints identical). Comment = the key's own SSH comment field.

| `aliwh_ed25519` | `gxCbcvRlRWoD0+QzyrHfGrq/yiwRD6bsDSDwSSLg3MU` | `id19y@outlook.com` | **passphrase** (aes256-ctr/bcrypt) |
| `aliwh_ed25519_root` | `rz90xzYmQgnLxXCsmKsbtgi9TecDWv0FqltlP9pi4Gg` | `root@sshwh.ccmii.eu.org` | **passphrase** (aes256-ctr/bcrypt) |

## Key → server mapping (inferred, needs your confirmation)

`config` only ever described one host, so this table was reconstructed from key names,
key comments and `server_list.txt`. Two rows are guesses; they are marked as such.

| `server_list.txt` entry | Likely key | Confidence |
|-------------------------|------------|------------|
| `sshwh.ccmii.eu.org:5419` user `y19` (aliwh) | `aliwh_ed25519` | high |
| `sshwh.ccmii.eu.org:5419` user `root` | `aliwh_ed25519_root` | high |
| `178.162.244.176:21054` root (奥地利家宽) | `id_ed25519` (comment `tmp`) | medium — see note |
| `103.136.185.169:2665` root (moe sjc) | `103.136.185.169_ed25519` **or** `moe_ed25519` | **TODO — ambiguous** |

**Note on the Austria entry.** `incomplete/austria_tmp` was not a corrupt key: it is a
byte-for-byte duplicate of `keys/id_ed25519` (both normalize to MD5 `0b1da3405d86ec1744d9ea73de999ea8`,
same fingerprint). The original "invalid format" report was the missing final newline
plus CRLF, not a damaged key. It has been removed as a duplicate. If `id_ed25519` really
is the Austria home-broadband key, that is the explanation — otherwise the true Austria
key was never backed up and `178.162.244.176` is protected by a password you have not
stored here. Worth checking against `C:\Users\19y\.ssh` on the source machine.

## Other files

- `server_list.txt` — host inventory (12 entries) **including plaintext passwords**; see Security notes.
- `config` — a single WSL-style entry: `Host 172.18.70.164` / port 2222 / user `debian19y`.
  It has no `IdentityFile` lines, so it does not map any of the ten keys. Regenerate a real
  config from the mapping table above before relying on it.

Deliberately excluded: `known_hosts` / `known_hosts.old` (host-trust cache, not identity).

## Restore (example)

```powershell
$dst = "$env:USERPROFILE\.ssh"
Copy-Item .\keys\* $dst\ -Force
Copy-Item .\config $dst\config -Force

# Private keys must not be readable by other users on Windows OpenSSH:
icacls "$dst\aliwh_ed25519" /inheritance:r /grant:r "${env:USERNAME}:R"

# Confirm the endings survived the copy (should print a fingerprint):
ssh-keygen -lf "$dst\aliwh_ed25519"
```

If you restore from a `git clone` on Windows, delete and re-clone (or run
`git add --renormalize .`) after pulling this commit, so the previously CRLF-converted
files are replaced by LF ones.
